🔥🇲🇽 <u>CDMX BUSTS HOME-THEFT RINGS — COPS AND OFFICIALS INSIDE</u>

Mexico City’s prosecutor’s office has dismantled two criminal networks dedicated to stealing homes — with public officials inside them: six police detained, ten more arrest warrants out.

The numbers: 1,846 investigation files from 1,966 complaints, and some 300 properties already returned to their owners under the current administration. The despojo networks are losing their protection.

🇲🇽⚒️ <u>PASTA DE CONCHOS: RESCUE NOW 70-85% COMPLETE</u>

Twenty years after Grupo México and the neoliberal state abandoned 65 miners underground, the rescue at Pasta de Conchos is advancing: 70%, 83% and 85% complete in the main work units. So far 36 bodies recovered, 31 identified, 28 returned to their families.

Labor Secretary Bolaños: "Faced with the abandonment these families endured for years, Mexican Humanism now puts people at the center, assumes the responsibility of finishing the rescue."

🇲🇽✈️ <u>MEXICANA DE AVIACIÓN: 20-AIRCRAFT FLEET BY 2027</u>

The state airline the neoliberals killed and the 4T brought back keeps growing: Mexicana de Aviación expects to close next year with a 20-aircraft fleet — seven new Embraer jets arriving this year, eight more in 2027.

In two years of operations it has sold over a million tickets, with 95% user satisfaction. The "failed" public airline is right on schedule.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>ONTARIO THANKS MEXICO: DOUG FORD EATS HIS WORDS</u>

Ontario Premier Doug Ford — who not long ago was making "not very good statements" about Mexico — just sent a letter thanking the country for the firefighters battling Canada’s wildfires.

Sheinbaum’s answer: "More than a strategic partner, Mexico is in solidarity with all countries... may solidarity and fraternity always be the hallmark of Mexico." While Washington threatens, Mexico sends firefighters.

‍UPI: Mexico's cartel fight requires partnership, not intervention July 31, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Rare for a Washington think-tank byline: CSIS's Evan Ellis argues in UPI against US military action in Mexico, credits Harfuch's security approach, and assigns the US co-responsibility for drug demand and weapons flows. 🔍 Still Washington-voiced — the "Mexican perspective" arrives via unnamed security specialists, no Mexican officials quoted. • "Mexico is not a state run by drug cartels." • "neither a helpless victim nor an enemy territory requiring American intervention"

‍REUTERS: Mexico arrests suspected gang leader accused of ordering mayor's killing July 30, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Reuters: Mexico arrests "El R1," alleged CJNG cell leader accused of ordering the assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo — 31 now held in the case, 10,500+ security forces deployed to Michoacán. 🇲🇽 Clean wire copy, but single-sourced to the security ministry; the teen suspect killed by security forces is stated, not examined. • "triggered protests against insecurity" • "deploying more than 10,500 security force members"

‍NACLA: Mexico Favors Israel for Weapons Imports July 29, 2026 | 🟢 📰 NACLA digs into Mexico's UN Arms Trade Treaty report: nearly 18,000 firearms bought from Israel in 2025 — 37% of all imports, triple the 2024 figure — with 63% going to military and civilian use. 🔍 Criticism of the 4T from the left for once, built on ATT data and SEDENA freedom-of-information receipts, not the usual Washington script. • "deepening ties with the genocidal state raises serious concerns" • "an alliance of forces that employ those weapons with impunity"

‍LATIN TIMES: Who Is Juan Carlos Valencia González, the Jalisco Cartel's Newly Confirmed Leader? July 28, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Latin Times: OFAC's biggest-ever CJNG sanctions round formally names Juan Carlos Valencia González, "El Pelón" — El Mencho's US-born stepson — as the cartel's new leader. $5M reward, indicted in 2020, ex-chief of the Grupo Élite hitmen. 🔍 Straight aggregation of OFAC, WSJ and Milenio sourcing; no current Mexican government or community voice. • "formally identified Valencia González as the new CJNG leader" • "serves as the CJNG's chief of hitmen and gunmen"

‍NYT: Mexico's President Unveils Plan to Fight Seaweed That Is Choking Beaches July 30, 2026 | 🟢 📰 NYT covers Sheinbaum's $115M sargassum plan straight: two 200-foot Navy ships hauling 3+ tons of seaweed a minute, 30 miles of barriers — as 9,000 tons a day hit Quintana Roo, 27x the historic average. 🇲🇽 The lens is tourism revenue (9% of GDP); what drives the blooms — warming seas — never comes up. • "a record-breaking scourge of seaweed that is spoiling vacations" • "one of the most pernicious threats to the nation's crucial tourism industry"
